config.purpose: Continuity (F6 of docs/EXECUTION-PLAN.md): one repository, a lending library's API, goes through ten sessions in the same directory while decisions are added (steps 2, 4, 9) and one replaces another (step 5). Each session is a new agent session; the user states a rule once, in the session where it is decided, and never repeats it. After each session the oracle judges the request and every decision in force, on the whole code.
config.subject: agent_harness
config.note: Decisions kept = AC-KEEP-* criteria passed over those judged at steps whose AC-REQUEST passed (38 when every request is done); report it with the steps passed. The two decisions recorded before the chain are in docs/decisions and in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, so every agent knows them; the rules stated later live only in the conversation, and each agent keeps them its own way. The simulated user approves a proposed decision whose title or rule matches the rule it stated in that session (its topic with the negation the user gave, or its idiom, such as soft delete) and declines any other; its veto list (declineDecisions) declines a proposal that inverts the rule or replaces it with another even when it also matches, and it declines a proposal that supersedes any decision but the one the user agreed to replace in that session (supersedeDecisions: D-0002 at step 5 only). Compare full Shelra with --ablate ledger on the same model, and with reference agents (claude-code, codex), k >= 3.

scorePolicy.note: Provisional development policy. Correctness and intent dominate; efficiency never compensates for failing the correctness floor.

tasks.prompt: Add book loans. POST /loans with a user_id and a book_id lends the book: answer 201 with the loan (its id, user id, book id, lent at, due at, which is 14 days after lent at, and returned at, which stays null until the book comes back), 404 when the user or the book does not exist, and 409 when the book is already out. POST /loans/:id/return records the return and answers 200 with the loan, or 404 for an unknown loan. GET /books/:id should also say whether the book is available right now, as available: true or false.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Books can be lent and returned, and a book says whether it is available.

tasks.prompt: Add DELETE /users/:id: answer 204, or 404 when there is no such user. This project never removes rows from its database: deleting a user sets its deleted_at column, and every endpoint then treats that user as if it did not exist (GET /users leaves them out, GET /users/:id and POST /loans answer 404). That is a rule for the whole project from now on, not only for this endpoint.
